Project Ares · Holotable symbology

Icon sheet

A snapshot of the icon sheet, kept for reference. It shows every symbol as the game draws it. The review version had comment and verdict controls and ran as a claude.ai page.

  1. LookLarge on the left of each card, then at the size the player actually sees. The bloom switch above shows them with and without glow.
  2. CommentPress Comment on a card and describe the change: shape, weight, size, color, meaning. Be as specific or loose as you like.
  3. VerdictKeep, Revise or Cut. It saves for everyone with the page open. Press the same button again to clear it.

Color key

  • Friendly #39C6FF

    Your ships, placed points, flip and arrival markers

  • Neutral #F2F5F7

    Independent ships and stations

  • Hostile #FF3344

    Enemy ships. Red always means danger

  • Threat #FF5A4A

    Hostile torpedoes, pulsing

  • Uncertain #FF7A1A

    Unknown contacts and warnings on the table

  • Our fire #3DF56B

    Our weapons once fired: impact marks

  • Their fire #FFE433

    Enemy weapons once fired: impact marks

  • Chrome #7C93A0

    Body markers and panel frames

  • Text #DCE6EA

    Selection reticle and labels

In the game

Where these symbols sit on the table. The icons are small and constant in size, so they read against grids, rings and labels rather than on a clean ground.

Ships and contacts 8 symbols

Allegiance is color plus treatment: plain outline for friendly and neutral, corner brackets for hostile, dashed for unknown. Filled means the drive is burning, hollow means coasting.

The family side by side

Line weight scales with the icon, from 1.1 px on the torpedo to 2.3 px on the capital ship. Quads run from 24 to 50 px.

Appears in Under every ship, contact, body and placed point

Drawn live in 3D, so on the table the ring is an ellipse that follows the camera. Built by hand here from its numbers, unlike the others.

Not on this sheet. The HUD buttons are text only today, so there are no HUD icons to review yet. Route lines, range rings, PDC tracers and the holotable frame are line work rather than icons.

The atlas also draws dashed versions of every ship class that nothing uses today, because only the unknown contact is dashed. They would come into play for stale contacts, and the dashes break up badly on the small chevrons.

Generated from src/render/symbolAtlas.ts. After revisions, npm run icons rebuilds this sheet.
